settings.name: str#3697
settings.resolved_name: Curve Shaper is an advanced overclocking tuning suite utilizing the same "Curve optimizer" steps. It changes variable voltage across all cores for finite (overlapping) frequency and temperature regions. This can be used to more precisely tune the voltage required by your system. In general, Low temperature corresponds to idle temps, Med Temperature corresponds to 1T/Gaming Workloads, and high temperature is for stress tests. Additionally, Min and Low frequencies are idle/background tasks, Medium is high core count workloads, and high and Max frequency are for gaming and 1T workloads. These settings work as "bands" so you may find that for particular cases several settings impact the behavior. Ex, A workload running at 65 Celsius will likely be influenced by Low temp and Med temp values. Workloads lower than 65C will be more impacted by Low. Workloads above 65C will be more impacted by Medium.

settings.name: str#3699
settings.resolved_name: Determines the direction of the shift. Positive shifts the curve up to use higher voltages. Negative shifts the curve down to use lower voltages

settings.name: str#3701

settings.resolved_name: Curve Shaper is an advanced overclocking tuning suite utilizing the same "Curve optimizer" steps. It changes variable voltage across all cores for finite (overlapping) frequency and temperature regions. This can be used to more precisely tune the voltage required by your system. In general, Low temperature corresponds to idle temps, Med Temperature corresponds to 1T/Gaming Workloads, and high temperature is for stress tests. Additionally, Min and Low frequencies are idle/background tasks, Medium is high core count workloads, and high and Max frequency are for gaming and 1T workloads. These settings work as "bands" so you may find that for particular cases several settings impact the behavior. Ex, A workload running at 65 Celsius will likely be influenced by Low temp and Med temp values. Workloads lower than 65C will be more impacted by Low. Workloads above 65C will be more impacted by Medium.
